question.text: SEBI regulatory fees on ETIRD transactions are:

answer.text: Paid by the exchange from its own funds
A component of the trading cost borne by market participants

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI turnover fee on ETIRD is a regulatory levy that forms part of trading costs and is recoverable from clients at actuals. The fee is payable to SEBI by the stock broker / clearing member / self-clearing member; the current rate applicable on IRD turnover is Rs. 5 per crore. The Trap: The exchange does not pay it from its own funds (option A), and it is not exempt for ETIRD (option C). It is also not borne only by clearing members -- it is recovered from the client (option D). Note: Workbook reference: NISM Series IV pp.222-223. The rate (Rs. 5 per crore) is set by SEBI and may be revised from time to time; always check the prevailing rate.
